sections.h2: Where is Southampton, and which part of it is your house in?
sections.html:
Southampton is a large town at the eastern end of Suffolk County, wrapped by the Atlantic Ocean on its south side and Peconic Bay on the north. It covers 293.46 square miles, but only 139.13 of those are land, and the rest is water. English settlers from Lynn, Massachusetts founded it in 1640, and the area is widely known as the Hamptons. The oldest surviving house, the Halsey House at 249 Main Street, was built by Thomas Halsey, one of the first Englishmen to trade with the Shinnecock, and the town keeps an online map of more than 100 historic markers and districts.

The town is a collection of smaller places, and the one on your deed matters more than the town name. Seven incorporated villages sit inside it: North Haven, Quogue, Sag Harbor (partly), Sagaponack, Southampton, Westhampton Beach and West Hampton Dunes. The unincorporated hamlets include Bridgehampton, East Quogue, Flanders, Hampton Bays, North Sea, Noyack, Remsenburg, Riverside, Shinnecock Hills, Speonk, Tuckahoe and Water Mill. A house in an incorporated village may answer to the village's own code office as well as the town.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about housing in Southampton?
sections.html:
Southampton is expensive, and many of its houses are lived in by owners who plan to stay. The latest five-year figures from the Census Bureau give a typical owner-occupied value of $928,100, with 82.4% of homes owner-occupied and 90.8% of residents in the same house a year earlier. Gross rent is typically $2,363 a month.

  • Estimated population on July 1, 2025: 71,601, up 3.7% from the 2020 base.
  • Residents aged 65 and over: 25.1%, compared with 18.4% in neighboring Smithtown town.
  • Households: 26,576, averaging 2.55 people.
  • Typical household income: $128,594.
  • Average commute: 29.8 minutes.

A value near $928,100 sits just under the $1 million line that triggers New York's extra mansion tax, so the exact sale price can change what the buyer owes at the closing table. Price your house with that threshold in mind.

sections.h2: How does Southampton's coastal weather affect an older house?
sections.html:
Southampton has a hot-summer humid continental climate bordering on humid subtropical. Climate normals for Bridgehampton show about 49.8 inches of precipitation a year and 26.8 inches of snow, with a January daily mean near 30.7 °F and a July mean near 72 °F.

With about 114 days of measurable precipitation a year and a shoreline on two sides, moisture is a fact of life for houses here. Keep receipts for roof, siding, drainage and mechanical work, and gather repair paperwork after any storm damage so a buyer's inspector can see what was done and when.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Southampton house that has been rented?
sections.html:
Yes, but the town's rental permit rules shape how you sell it. Any dwelling rented for any period needs a rental permit, and the Town Code sets a minimum stay of 14 days. Shorter stays count as transient rentals, which the code does not allow. There is no maximum stay.

Southampton rental permit rules, from the Town of Southampton's rental permit FAQ
QuestionTown answer
Is a permit needed?Yes, for any home rented for any period
Minimum stay14 days
How long is a permit good?Two years
Does it transfer to a new owner?No, a new owner needs a new permit
Processing timeAbout 1 to 3 weeks, 2 to 4 in summer
Where are applications dropped off?27 Ponquogue Ave., Hampton Bays

Because permits do not pass to a buyer, an investor purchasing a rental will have to apply in their own name, and moving a property into an LLC, trust or estate also requires a new permit. Advertising a house for rent without a permit can bring violations, suspension or revocation, and a two-year ban on renting. There are two routes to a permit. A Standard application is inspected by a New York State certified code enforcement officer from the town's Department of Public Safety. A Certified application uses an architect or engineer the owner hires, and expedited processing is also offered. An owner of a single-family house may rent up to two bedrooms to no more than two renters without a permit, as long as the owner lives there and everyone shares the kitchen and living space.

sections.h2: When do Southampton property taxes come due?
sections.html:
The Town Receiver of Taxes mails bills by December 15, and half is due by January 10 with the second half due by May 31. Payment can be made in person, online or by mail with a postmark on or before the due date. Online, an e-check costs $1.75 and credit cards add a 2.5% fee charged by the processor.

Late payments are costly. Taxes paid after January 10 can still go to the Receiver, with 1% interest added each month. After May 31 a 5% penalty plus 5% interest applies, and the town can no longer accept payment; the balance goes to the Suffolk County Treasurer's Office in Riverhead at 631-852-3000.

  • Exemption applications, including STAR and the senior, veterans and disability exemptions, are due March 1.
  • Grievance Day is the third Tuesday in May, and the Assessor's Office at 116 Hampton Road can help at 631-283-6020.
  • Property details and amounts due are searchable on the town's eTax portal by address, owner's last name, tax map number or bill number, and a duplicate bill can be requested there.
  • Unpaid taxes are not ignored: the county typically starts collection on vacant land after one year and on improved property after three.

Your closing figures will credit or charge each side for the part of the tax year they owned the house, so ask for current balances before the contract date.

sections.h2: What transfer taxes and forms apply to a Southampton deed?
sections.html:
Southampton sellers deal with the state's transfer tax, while buyers deal with a local charge. The state tax is $2 for each $500 of price, paid by the seller, and at $928,100 it comes to $3,714. A buyer pays the 1% mansion tax only if the residential price reaches $1 million.

The town also runs the Community Preservation Fund, which is financed by a two percent real estate transfer tax. The town's housing fund FAQ describes that fee as one paid by the purchaser, not the seller. At recording, the county clerk requires a Peconic Bay Region Community Preservation form with every recording in the five East End towns, which are Riverhead, Southampton, East Hampton, Shelter Island and Southold. Both parties sign it.

Deeds are recorded by the Suffolk County Clerk in Riverhead, together with the RP-5217 transfer report and TP-584 return. Deed forms are not sold by the clerk, and every party needs a street address on the deed, not a P.O. box.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental permit to sell a Southampton house I rented out?
faqs.a: A permit is not required to sell, but it is required to rent. Permits last two years and cannot be passed to a buyer, so the new owner applies for their own.

faqs.q: How much interest is added if Southampton taxes are late?
faqs.a: After January 10, first-half taxes accrue 1% interest per month. After May 31 a 5% penalty and 5% interest apply, and the balance is collected by the Suffolk County Treasurer.

faqs.q: Who pays the Community Preservation Fund fee on a Southampton sale?
faqs.a: The buyer. The town describes its Community Preservation Fund transfer fee as paid by the purchaser, and the clerk requires the Peconic Bay Region form from both parties.

faqs.q: Can I rent my Southampton house for a weekend?
faqs.a: Not under the town code. The minimum rental stay is 14 days, and anything shorter counts as a transient rental that is not allowed.

faqs.q: When is the deadline for Southampton tax exemptions?
faqs.a: March 1 is the deadline for first-time exemption filings, including STAR, senior, veterans and disability exemptions. Applications go to the Assessor's Office.
